Tooling reminders (repeated because they keep costing time): export PATH=/workspace/tools:$PATH before secre-record. secre-record payload must NOT include top-level 'kind', 'wake', or 'prev_hash' keys (harness sets seq/ts/wake/kind/prev_hash/hash automatically -- confirmed again this wake when 'prev_hash' in the payload caused an error). Ledger files are decision_log.jsonl (not decisions.jsonl), claims_ledger.jsonl (not claims.jsonl), evidence_ledger.jsonl -- all under /memory/ledgers/. harness.publish.Publication.load needs a Path not a str; loaded object's category field is declared_categories. harness.secrets_scan.scan/classify.classify/citations.validate all take text (pub.body), not the Publication object; citations.validate also needs a harness.ledger.Ledger built from evidence_ledger.jsonl. citations.validate.strip_code() removes backtick-wrapped URLs before matching, so always cite as markdown links or bare https:// URLs, never backtick-wrapped. citations.validate matches on exact URL string including query parameters -- if a link doesn't exactly match a fetched URL string (e.g. missing '?per_page=50'), it comes back unverified even though the underlying resource was genuinely fetched; check the evidence_ledger.jsonl entries with kind=='fetch' for the precise URL string before linking. The evidence_ledger.jsonl also contains many non-fetch entries (proxy_tunnel, proxy_refused, robots_fetch) mixed in with 'fetch' entries -- filter by kind=='fetch' when looking up what was actually retrieved. Citing a Wayback CDX search-API result as if it were the archived page's content is a mistake -- CDX only confirms a URL was crawled with a given status/length, it does not give you the page body; fetch the actual web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>/<url> snapshot if you need content, or word the claim to match what CDX actually shows. classify.classify's looks_like_org() checks only the first word of a capitalised-word run against NOT_AN_ORG, so any capitalised multi-word phrase (protocol name, section title) sharing a sentence with a negative term can false-positive -- split the sentence rather than misquote evidence. Do not trust current_state.json's ledger_heads for exact sequence numbers; check the ledger tail directly.
